outcome.technical: CHANGES. (a) .github/sweep-costs.json re-recorded from Windows CI logs, fixing review finding P143-R6. Logs: all 8 Windows selftests cells of release-tier run 41070108164 at d1a877b7 (plain 1-4, cp1252 1-4, jobs 124111662040/138/498/607/692/813/921/936, all green). Each log was fetched with `gh api repos/AleksandarBisevac/claude-plugins/actions/jobs/<id>/logs`, because `gh run view --log` refuses while the resample job is still running. The logs were concatenated and recorded with `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <all.log> --platform windows-2025 --workers 4 --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`. Exit 0, output: recorded 193 files' seconds and 324 blocks'. The value 4 comes from each cell's `budget: 4 slots` line. The table is now entirely Windows measurement with no darwin figures left over. A separate recording into an empty scratch table produced the same file byte for byte (cmp IDENTICAL), and its file and block key sets match the old table with nothing missing on either side. Table platform is windows-2025, workers 4. Total slot-seconds went from 2477 (darwin) to 7978 (windows). test__manifest_io went 4.4 -> 132.5. Heaviest block: test_drive_phase ar18-block at 182.4. (b) tools/gate-parity.py: added MANIFEST_WORK, manifest_work_slices(), per_run_named(), family_shard_parts() and WINDOWS_SHARDS, plus selftest cases sv13-sv15 via _ci_shape_cases(), which runs after _slice_cases. sv13 is the live claim, read against the real ci.yml and the real `verify.sh --list`. It checks three things: every slice a per-run job names is listed; each manifest-validation piece (validator, sharded layout, doctor, report smoke, rendered artifacts) is run by a per-run job, with pieces found by the command words --list prints rather than by slice name; and the Windows sweep cells run parts 1..4 of 4 for every Windows slice. sv14 covers three fixtures that must each be reported: an unlisted `manifests-doctor`, the manifests slice dropped, and the manifests slice moved to the release-tier job only. sv15 covers two more: the matrix narrowed to 3 of 3 (which shard_matrix_drift accepts) and an exclude that drops part 4 on Windows. (c) .github/workflows/ci.yml: comment only. The re-record recipe used to name the floating `windows-latest` and omitted `--workers`, so the table would record workers null. It now names windows-2025 and --workers <slots>, and says to fetch logs through the API while the run is in progress. NOT CHANGED, AND WHY: tools/verify.sh is unchanged. The task asked to split the manifest-validation job into parallel slices, and I did not do that, on the measured evidence. In run 41070108164 the manifest-validation steps took 18 s (log timestamps 14:14:46 -> 14:15:04) inside a 49 s 'manifests + js + plugin' job. In run 40946289828 that job took 56 s. The critical path is the Windows sweep cells (453-581 s). Each extra job adds its own checkout + setup-python + setup-node + npm ci (14:14:33 -> 14:14:45 = 12 s of setup in this run) to runner-minutes and moves wall clock by 0 s, so a split works against acceptance (1). 'Windows on four shards' was already in HEAD's ci.yml (shard: [1, 2, 3, 4] crossed with both OS values); sv13 now locks it. MEASURED, RUN 41070108164 (one run; per-run jobs, resample excluded; raw job durations from `gh run view 41070108164 --json jobs`): per-run runner-minutes 106.3; wall 9.9 min from the first job start to the last end. Breakdown: the 8 Windows cells sum to 66.6 min, the 8 linux cells to 23.0, the browser jobs to 12.6, the rest to about 4. The Windows cells ran with the old darwin-balanced split (619 slot-s per part on darwin figures) and finished 453-581 s apart within a leg. Re-balanced on the new Windows table, `--shard 1/4` prints 1994 / 1994 / 1994 / 1994 slot-seconds per part; over 4 slots that is about 498 s of sweep per cell plus about 60 s of setup. WHAT THE NEXT CI RUNS MUST SHOW, which I cannot claim: (1) a median of at least five per-run runs at or under 8 min wall and 55 runner-minutes. 55 runner-minutes cannot be reached by job shape. The 8 Windows cells alone measured 66.6 runner-minutes, and dropping the Windows cp1252 leg (34.8) and the linux stress leg (11.6) would still leave about 60. Meeting the target needs the sweep's own CPU cut, or a decision to drop legs, which is the owner's call (ci.yml says the cp1252 deletion waits on evidence). (2) The manifest work is already 18 s, so it is met. (3) shard_matrix_drift and gate-parity are green locally (see below). (4) The table's recorded date is this change's commit date; the table carries no date field. CHECKS RUN: `python3 tools/gate-parity.py --selftest` exit 0, ALL PASS 97/97 (94 before, plus sv13, sv14, sv15). `python3 tools/gate-parity.py` exit 0 (13 slices, 8 jobs). Mutation probe at <scratchpad>/probe/mutations.py, output beside it in <scratchpad>/probe/mutations.out (exit 0, '10 row(s), 0 not as expected'). Each row runs on a scratch copy of the working tree, asserts its anchor appears exactly once and that the mutation landed, purges __pycache__, and restores in finally. On the first pass m2 (release-tier jobs counted as per-run) SURVIVED, so sv14 gained the moved-to-release fixture, and after that every row was KILLED. That includes three over-fire rows (m7-m9) that turn the live allow case sv13 red. The plan gate REFUSED writing probe/mutations.py in the checkout, verbatim: '[require-plan] Outside the running plan (change magnitude 142 (> 80)): probe/mutations.py ... No task in docs/audit/audit-plan.json declares probe/mutations.py'. That is why the probe lives in the scratchpad and runs against a copy. DEPENDANTS: .github/sweep-costs.json -> ci.yml: path reference, still correct. stamp-verification.py: its sweep_wall budget now reads Windows figures, about 3.2x the darwin sum, so on a dev machine a sweep-shaped red-first command holds back more time for the fix run. tests/test_stamp_verification.py run through the sweep: exit 0, 1/1 files, 352 cases. tools/sweep-selftests.py: `--selftest` exit 0, 156/156. Heaviest block timeout is 3 x 182.4 = 547 s, under SWEEP_DEADLINE 1800. CHANGELOG/CLAUDE/CONTRIBUTING/PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE: grep shows only path and semantics references and no figures, still correct. tools/verify.sh: unchanged, so its dependants are unaffected. ci.yml -> affected.py, _harness, test__impact, test__manifest_phases, test__refs, test_audit_task, test_drive_phase, audit-task.py: only a comment changed, it names no new tool basename, and no runs-on, matrix or job was touched, so all still correct. gate-parity.py -> the new names take required arguments and end in no lint suffix (_violations, _drift or _claims), so prove-gates derives no new lint; `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --list` exit 0, no unrowed entry. ruff exit 0, vermin exit 0, house_style_violations/prose_number_claims report nothing for gate-parity.py. FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: (i) within run 41070108164, tests/test__impact.py took 7.8 s on one leg and 30.8 s on the other, a 3.9x spread. That is above TIMEOUT_PER_COST 3, which tools/sweep-selftests.py's comment says sits over the observed spread (not my file). (ii) ci.yml's 'longest selftests: 13m35s (estimate)' cannot be replaced by this run's measured 9m41s while the bound stays 33: 3 x 9m41s is 29m03s, under 33. The bound is tied to SWEEP_DEADLINE in tools/sweep-selftests.py, outside my files. (iii) tools/sweep-selftests.py:10's docstring example still shows `--platform win32` with no --workers (not my file). Note: I briefly started an unintended `sweep-selftests.py --shard 1/4 --list` loop. --list is not a sweep flag, so it ran a shard. I killed it with pkill; git status showed no strays afterwards.
outcome.descriptive: The sweep cost table now holds Windows measurements, and gate-parity locks Windows on four parts and the manifest-validation work to a per-run job. I declined the manifest split: it is 18 s off the critical path and would only add runner-minutes. 55 runner-minutes cannot be reached by job shape (Windows cells alone are 66.6).
